fi-melanotaenia-herbertaxelrodi.title: Herbert Axelrod's Rainbowfish
fi-melanotaenia-herbertaxelrodi.summary: The Lake Tebera rainbowfish, Melanotaenia herbertaxelrodi, is a rainbowfish endemic to the Lake Tebera basin in the Central Highlands of New Guinea. It inhabits clear, heavily vegetated water in the…
rows: shoal of at least 6-8, preferably more.
Omnivore. Like most of its congeners it's an unfussy, omnivorous species, and will accept most dried, frozen and live foods.
notes: This rainbowfish is ideally suited to a heavily planted setup and will show its best colours in such surroundings.
Water flow should be quite slow and this will also benefit the plants.

fi-glossolepis-incisus.title: Red Irian Rainbowfish
fi-glossolepis-incisus.summary: The red rainbowfish, Glossolepis incisus, is a rainbowfish from the Lake Sentani region of northern New Guinea, Indonesia. Also known as the salmon-red or New Guinea rainbowfish, it is usually found…
rows: shoal of at least 6-8 fish, preferably more.
Unfussy and will accept most dried, frozen and live foods.
Indonesia, specifically the Lake Sentani region of Northern New Guinea.
notes: This species, like most rainbows, looks most at home in a planted aquarium.
Provide areas of dense vegetation, along with some open areas for swimming.

fi-melanotaenia-boesemani.title: Boesemani Rainbow
fi-melanotaenia-boesemani.summary: Boeseman's rainbowfish, Melanotaenia boesemani, is a rainbowfish from Indonesia, known only from the Ajamaru lakes and nearby Lakes Hain and Aitinjo. One of the most popular rainbowfish in the hobby,…
rows: shoal of at least 6-8, preferably more.
Omnivore. Unfussy and will accept most dried, frozen and live foods.
notes: This species, like most rainbows, looks most at home in a planted aquarium.
Provide areas of dense vegetation, along with some open areas for swimming.

fi-melanotaenia-lacustris.title: Turquoise Rainbow
fi-melanotaenia-lacustris.summary: The Lake Kutubu rainbowfish, Melanotaenia lacustris, is a rainbowfish endemic to Lake Kutubu and the River Soro in Papua New Guinea. The lake is threatened by overfishing, much of it for the aquarium…
rows: shoal of at least 6-8, preferably more.
Omnivore. Like most of its congeners, it's an unfussy, omnivorous species and will accept most dried, frozen and live foods.
Papua New Guinea, Southern Highlands Province.
notes: This species, like most rainbows, looks most at home in a planted aquarium.
Provide areas of dense vegetation, along with some open areas for swimming.

fi-melanotaenia-parkinsoni.title: Parkinsoni Rainbow
fi-melanotaenia-parkinsoni.summary: Melanotaenia parkinsoni, the orange rainbowfish, is a species of rainbowfish in the subfamily Melanotaeniinae. It endemic to the western lakes of Papua New Guinea, [ 1 ] specifically the Kemp…
rows: Up to about 11.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-bedotia-geayi.title: Madagascar Rainbow
fi-bedotia-geayi.summary: The red-tailed silverside, or zona ( Bedotia geayi) is a species of Madagascar rainbowfish endemic to the Mananjary River drainage in Madagascar. Zona are threatened by both habitat loss and…
rows: Up to about 9.0 cm TL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-melanotaenia-splendida.title: Australian Rainbow
fi-melanotaenia-splendida.summary: Melanotaenia splendida, the Eastern rainbowfish, is a species of rainbowfish from the subfamily Melanotaeniinae which is found in Australia.
rows: Up to about 20.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)

fi-telmatherina-ladigesi.title: Celebese Rainbow
fi-telmatherina-ladigesi.summary: Celebese Rainbow (Telmatherina ladigesi) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 8.0 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)
notes: [ edit ] The Celebes rainbowfish is a peaceful aquarium fish.
[ edit ] Marosatherina ladigesi is found only near the town of Maros from which the genus name Marosatherina is derived.

fi-melanotaenia-kamaka.title: Dwarf Kamaka Rainbow
fi-melanotaenia-kamaka.summary: Dwarf Kamaka Rainbow (Melanotaenia kamaka) for freshwater aquariums.
rows: Up to about 6.1 cm SL male/unsexed (FishBase max)
notes: [ edit ] This species adapts well to captivity, and is a social fish that needs members of its own species to feel safe.

fi-melanotaenia-praecox.title: Neon Dwarf Rainbowfish
fi-melanotaenia-praecox.summary: A small, peaceful rainbowfish from the Mamberamo river system of northern New Guinea. It shows its best color in a well-planted tank with floating plants to soften the light.
rows: About 2–3 in (FishBase: 5 cm SL; Seriously Fish: up to 80 mm SL)
Shoal of at least 6–8, more is better
Omnivore. Takes dried, frozen and live foods; regular live foods bring out the best color
Mamberamo River system, New Guinea (Indonesia): fast tributaries and nearby swamps
notes: Plant heavily and add floating plants to soften the light, but leave open lanes where males can display.
Needs clean water: plan on weekly partial water changes.

fi-chilatherina-alleni.title: Allen's Rainbowfish (Wapoga)
fi-chilatherina-alleni.summary: A New Guinea rainbowfish with a dark blue side stripe and reddish fins in males. Colors vary a lot by collecting site; the Wapoga River form has been in the hobby since 2012.
rows: Up to about 4 in (10 cm), usually under 2.75 in (7 cm)
In the wild: small crustaceans, ants and other insects, and aquatic insect larvae
Northern West Papua (Indonesia): streams between Nabire and the Wapoga River
notes: Wild habitat is slow-to-moderate streams over gravel or sand with leaf litter and logs, often in sunny stretches.
Males grow larger and deeper-bodied than females, with longer, pointed rear fins.
